subject.title: fix(exec): require approval for OpenClaw lifecycle commands

question: Should OpenClaw adopt this explicit lifecycle-command taxonomy as a security boundary for all non-yolo exec approval paths after the implementation is split into the existing command-analysis architecture?
rationale: The remaining choice is not a mechanical test repair: it defines which gateway and daemon operations receive stronger confirmation and therefore sets a durable compatibility and security policy.

options.title: Adopt the boundary after extraction
options.body: Require the classifier to move into a focused internal analysis module, pass the max-lines guard, and provide final-head runtime proof before accepting the listed lifecycle taxonomy.

options.title: Narrow the boundary
options.body: Limit the first version to a smaller set of canonical OpenClaw lifecycle entrypoints and track carrier-specific expansion separately.

options.title: Pause the direction
options.body: Keep the existing approval model until a maintainer-approved lifecycle policy specification defines the supported command forms and exclusions.

recommendation.title: Adopt the boundary after extraction
recommendation.body: Require the classifier to move into a focused internal analysis module, pass the max-lines guard, and provide final-head runtime proof before accepting the listed lifecycle taxonomy.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main history ties this person most directly to the approval-model and command-analysis design that the new boundary extends.
